$comment: Identity is frozen by artifacts/design/rule-catalog-v1.md. Fields here must match it field-for-field; scripts/rule-identity.mjs enforces that. Where a requirement is informed by an external criterion, the citation lives in the standard's prose as a token and in artifacts/external-standards-provenance.json — never here, because a catalog field that carried an external conformance level would invite deriving a local level from it.

rules.title: Images carry an appropriate text alternative
rules.description: An image conveying information carries a text alternative describing that information. A decorative image is marked as decorative rather than given an invented description.
rules.rationale: An image without an alternative is absent for anyone not seeing it, and a decorative image described anyway is noise that makes the real content harder to find.
rules.remediation: Add an alt attribute describing the image's purpose, or mark it decorative with an empty alt.
rules.$assuranceNote: Source analysis finds images whose alternative is missing. Whether a present alternative is appropriate is a judgment no scan makes, and images produced dynamically are not enumerable from source.

rules.title: Interactive elements have accessible names
rules.description: Every control exposes a name to assistive technology that describes what it does.
rules.rationale: A control with no name is announced as its role alone. 'Button' is not an action a user can decide to take.
rules.remediation: Give the control visible text, or an aria-label or aria-labelledby that names its action.
rules.$assuranceNote: The computed accessible name depends on the rendered accessibility tree, so this is established only for the routes and states a browser run actually exercised.

rules.title: Headings express document structure without skipped levels
rules.description: Heading levels describe the document's real hierarchy and descend without skipping a level. Headings are not selected for their visual size.
rules.rationale: Heading navigation is a primary way screen-reader users move through a page, and a hierarchy chosen for appearance describes a structure the page does not have.
rules.remediation: Choose the heading level the content's position requires and style it separately.
rules.$assuranceNote: Level skips are detectable only within a single complete document. A page assembled from components at runtime has no source in which its heading sequence exists.

rules.title: Page regions are identified by landmarks
rules.description: The major regions of a page — primary navigation, main content, complementary content — are identified so they can be reached directly.
rules.rationale: Without landmarks the only way to reach the main content is to traverse everything before it, on every page.
rules.remediation: Use the semantic sectioning elements, or explicit landmark roles where the markup cannot carry them.
rules.$assuranceNote: Source analysis sees the landmarks a template declares, not the composed page a user receives.

rules.title: Data tables carry header semantics
rules.description: A table presenting data declares its header cells and their scope, so a cell can be announced with the headers that give it meaning.
rules.rationale: A data cell read without its column and row headers is a value with no subject.
rules.remediation: Mark header cells as headers and declare their scope, or use the equivalent grid semantics.
rules.$assuranceNote: Whether a table presents data or is used for layout is inferable from source only imperfectly, so this reports on tables it can classify.

rules.title: Content reflows under zoom and text scaling
rules.description: Content remains readable and operable when magnified or when the user enlarges text, without requiring scrolling in two directions to read a line.
rules.rationale: Magnification is the most common assistive adaptation there is, and an interface that breaks under it excludes users who need nothing else.
rules.remediation: Use layouts that reflow rather than fixed dimensions expressed in absolute units.
rules.$assuranceNote: Reflow is a property of resolved layout. It is established for the viewports and routes a browser run exercised and for nothing else.

rules.title: Contrast meets the project's declared target
rules.description: Text and meaningful non-text elements meet the contrast ratio their declared accessibility target requires, in every theme the project ships.
rules.rationale: Contrast failures are invisible to the person who authored them and disabling to the person who encounters them.
rules.remediation: Adjust the foreground or background token until the ratio meets the declared target, in every theme.
rules.$assuranceNote: A contrast ratio is computable only after the cascade resolves and the element renders. Source values do not determine it: a token can be overridden, inherited, or composited against an unexpected background.

rules.title: Time-based media carries alternatives
rules.description: Audio and video carrying information provide an alternative — captions, a transcript, or a description — appropriate to what the medium conveys.
rules.rationale: Media without alternatives is unavailable to users who cannot hear it or cannot see it, and to anyone who cannot play it.
rules.remediation: Attach captions or a transcript, and describe visual information the audio does not carry.
rules.$assuranceNote: Source analysis sees whether a track or transcript is declared. Whether it is accurate or complete is not machine-decidable.

rules.title: Functionality is operable by keyboard
rules.description: Every action available by pointer is available by keyboard, and no sequence traps focus in a component that cannot be left.
rules.rationale: Keyboard operation is the substrate every other assistive technology builds on. An action reachable only by pointer is unavailable, not merely inconvenient.
rules.remediation: Give the control real focusability and key handling, or replace it with an element that has both.
rules.$assuranceNote: Operability is established by driving the interface. A browser run establishes it for the flows it drove; unexercised flows remain unevaluated rather than passing.

rules.title: Keyboard focus is visibly indicated
rules.description: The element with keyboard focus is visibly distinguishable at every point in a keyboard traversal, including inside dialogs, menus, and custom components.
rules.rationale: A keyboard user who cannot see where focus is cannot use the interface at all, however operable it technically is.
rules.remediation: Provide a focus style with sufficient contrast against every background the element appears on.
rules.$assuranceNote: Whether an indicator is visible depends on resolved styles and the background it lands on. The static rule accessibility.no-removed-focus-indicators covers only the deliberate-removal case.

rules.title: Focus order follows meaning and stays unobscured
rules.description: Focus moves in an order that matches the interface's meaning, and the focused element is never hidden behind sticky, overlaid, or off-screen content.
rules.rationale: An order that contradicts the visual sequence makes the interface unpredictable, and a focused element behind a header is focus a user cannot find.
rules.remediation: Order the document to match meaning rather than reordering visually, and reserve space for fixed elements.
rules.$assuranceNote: Both halves need rendering: order depends on the composed document, and obscuring depends on resolved layout and stacking.

rules.title: Tab order is not overridden by positive tabindex
rules.description: A positive tabindex value is not used to impose a tab order.
rules.rationale: A positive value removes the element from the document's order and puts it in a separate sequence ahead of everything else, which makes the resulting order a property of scattered numbers rather than of the page.
rules.remediation: Remove the positive value and order the document so the natural sequence is the intended one.
rules.$assuranceNote: Attributes computed at runtime are invisible to source analysis, so absence of a finding is not proof that no positive value is ever set.

rules.title: Dialogs manage focus on open, during, and on close
rules.description: A modal dialog moves focus into itself when it opens, keeps focus within itself while open, and returns focus to a sensible place when it closes.
rules.rationale: A dialog that does not take focus is invisible to a keyboard user, and one that does not restore it strands them somewhere they did not choose.
rules.remediation: Move focus on open, contain it while open, and restore it to the invoking control on close.
rules.$assuranceNote: Focus containment is only observable by driving the dialog. Source shows that handlers exist, not that they behave.

rules.title: ARIA is used validly
rules.description: Roles, states, and properties are real, are used on elements that support them, and do not contradict what the element is. Hiding an interactive element from assistive technology while leaving it operable is one instance of this rule.
rules.rationale: Invalid ARIA does not degrade to no ARIA. It replaces a correct native semantic with an incorrect declared one, which is worse than having declared nothing.
rules.remediation: Use the native element whose semantics you are describing, or correct the role and its required properties.
rules.$assuranceNote: The detector recognises unknown roles and interactive elements hidden from assistive technology. It does not compute whether a valid role's required properties are all present in the composed element.

rules.title: Pointer targets meet a minimum size
rules.description: A control's activation area is large enough to be hit reliably, or has enough spacing around it that a near miss does not activate something else.
rules.rationale: Small adjacent targets turn ordinary imprecision into unintended actions, which is worst exactly where the consequence is destructive.
rules.remediation: Increase the target's padding or hit area, or increase the spacing between adjacent targets.
rules.$assuranceNote: Rendered size is not a source property. Declared dimensions say nothing about the box a user actually gets.

rules.title: Custom controls do not replace semantics with nothing
rules.description: A custom control built from generic elements does not ship without the role, state, and keyboard behavior the native control it replaces would have provided.
rules.rationale: Replacing a native control removes semantics that were free and correct. Shipping the replacement without restoring them is a net removal of accessibility, which is why no exception exists.
rules.remediation: Use the native control, or supply the role, the states it must expose, and full keyboard operation.
rules.$assuranceNote: Findings here are labeled INFERRED: source can show that a click handler sits on a non-interactive element, not that the resulting component is unusable.

rules.title: Focus indication is not removed
rules.description: A focus outline is not suppressed without a replacement indicator in its place.
rules.rationale: Removing focus indication is almost always done for appearance and always costs keyboard users the ability to tell where they are. There is no version of this trade that is worth making, which is why it is non-exemptible rather than a judgment call.
rules.remediation: Replace the default outline with a designed indicator rather than removing it.
rules.$assuranceNote: The detector reports suppression with no compensating style in the same file. A replacement declared elsewhere in the cascade is not visible to it, and whether a replacement is adequate needs rendering.

rules.title: Critical state is not encoded by color alone
rules.description: Error, success, selection, required status, and other state a user must act on is conveyed by something in addition to color.
rules.rationale: Color-only encoding is invisible to a substantial share of users and to anyone in conditions the designer did not have. The information is not degraded for them — it is absent.
rules.remediation: Add an icon, a text label, a shape, or a position that carries the same distinction.
rules.$assuranceNote: Which states are critical, and whether a second channel actually carries the distinction, is a design judgment. No scan makes it.

rules.title: Platform accessibility is not deliberately disabled
rules.description: Accessibility affordances the platform provides for free — user scaling and zoom among them — are not switched off.
rules.rationale: This is distinct from failing to build something accessible. It is taking away a capability the platform already gave the user, which no product requirement justifies.
rules.remediation: Remove the scaling restriction and fix the layout that motivated it.
rules.$assuranceNote: The detector recognises viewport declarations that disable user scaling. Other platform affordances a project might disable are not enumerable from source.
